title: Request and response bodies

richText: A request body contains data sent by the client, separate from the URL and headers.
@RequestBody asks a message converter to read the body into a Java argument.
For JSON, deserialization means converting JSON into Java data.
Content-Type identifies the format the client sends. For a JSON body, use application/json.
A DTO is a data transfer object. A request DTO declares the fields the API accepts.
A body is required by default. Invalid JSON or data that cannot be converted normally produces a 400 response.
A request DTO can be a Java record or a class supported by the configured JSON converter. Getters and setters are not the only supported design.
@ResponseBody asks a message converter to write the returned Java value into the response body.
@RestController applies this behavior to its handler methods.
Serialization means converting Java data into a format such as JSON.
Accept tells the server which response formats the client can read. The server must have a suitable converter.
Returning a String usually sends text. Return a data object when the API expects a JSON object.

example.title: Read JSON and return a JSON object
description: Use Java 17 or later with a Spring Boot MVC application that has JSON conversion configured.
Save UserRequest.java and UserController.java as separate files in a scanned package.
Send POST /users/echo with Content-Type: application/json and body {"name":"Alice","age":30}.
explanation: The JSON converter creates a UserRequest from the request body.
The controller returns that object. The response converter writes its fields as JSON.
consumes restricts the request format. produces declares the response format.
This endpoint echoes the input. It does not validate or save a user.
The JSON fields have the shown values; formatting and field order can differ.

richText: A handler can receive a JSON @RequestBody and separate query parameters. Their order in the method signature does not control conversion.
Validation of the converted data is a separate step, covered on the request validation page.

summary: Convert an HTTP body to Java data, then write Java data back to the response.
